items.title: Buss Family To Sell Remaining Stake In Lakers To Kushner, Iger
items.summary: After controlling owner Mark Walter agreed to sell his majority stake in the Lakers to Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger, the Buss family is following suit and will sell its remaining minority shares to the incoming ownership group, reports Shams Charania of ESPN (Twitter link). Jeanie Buss, Jim Buss, Johnny Buss, Janie Buss, Joey Buss, and Jesse Buss still owned 17.8% of the franchise. According to Charania, in order to enact the “tag-along provision” and sell that 17.8% stake at the same $12.5 billion valuation that Walter got in his agreement with Kushner and Iger, at least four of the six siblings had to vote in favor of selling. “We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction,” the siblings said in a statement to ESPN (Twitter link). “We love the Lakers, Laker fans and will continue to support Los…

items.title: Buss family selling remaining 17.8% ownership stake in Lakers to new majority owners Josh Kushner and Bob Iger
items.summary: After nearly 50 years, the Buss family will no longer be part of the Lakers’ ownership group. In a statement to ESPN, the family announced that it has chosen to sell its remaining 17.8% ownership stake in the Lakers to the new majority ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner, according to multiple reports.Iger and Kushner purchased the controlling stake in the Lakers last week for a record-breaking $12.5 billion."We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction. items.title: NBA blasts ESPN for ‘inaccuracies’ in report on Kawhi Leonard-Clippers investigation
items.summary: Kawhi Leonard is a seven-time All-Star.Photograph: Matt Slocum/APThe NBA has disputed an ESPN report on the league’s investigation into possible salary cap circumvention by the Los Angeles Clippers.On Monday, ESPN reported that, after an 11-month investigation, the NBA was not able to show proof that Clippers owner Steve Ballmer funneled money to Kawhi Leonard via team sponsorships to bypass the salary cap. items.summary: Haywood Highsmith will re-sign with the Suns, league sources tell Michael Scotto of HoopsHype (Twitter link). It will be a one-year contract, agent Jerry Dianis confirms to ESPN’s Shams Charania (Twitter link). The veteran forward was waived last Wednesday after spending just a few months with the team, and he became a free agent after clearing waivers on Friday. He held a $1MM guarantee on his $3MM contract for the upcoming season. Highsmith missed most of last season after undergoing surgery on a torn meniscus in his right knee last August and suffering a setback in his rehab in October. He signed a two-year, minimum-salary contract with Phoenix in February and appeared in seven regular season games and two playoff contests. items.title: And-Ones: D’Antoni, Buss Brothers, Hartenstein, Hall Of Famers
items.summary: Mike D’Antoni was inducted into the Hall of Fame this weekend as part of the 2026 class. He knows that the primary reason he’s getting in is the philosophical change in the league that he helped usher in when he brought the “Seven Seconds or Less” philosophy over from his coaching days in Italy, ESPN’s Dave McMenamin writes. While D’Antoni’s Suns’ up-and-down, free-flowing offense influenced the way that teams play today, he still regrets that he didn’t push the style even further, closer to what it has become today. “Because we were first to go through the door, first of all, you take a lot of bullets. And … it makes you hesitate. We didn’t go as far as we could have pushed the envelope back then because we didn’t know,” D’Antoni said. “We’d shoot 30-something threes and we’re going, ‘Is that too many?
